plan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique, orthographic-style layout with a broad cuboid matching the source: no perspective convergence. World-space layout: left cuboid front x_1-x_2 face is about 5.8 units wide by 4.6 units high; latent z depth is about 3.8 units, drawn as a receding diagonal offset of about +1.9 units screen-right and -1.0 units screen-down. In source-axis terms, +X is x_1 screen-right across the cuboid front face, +Y is x_2 screen-up along the left vertical edge, and +Z is the receding oblique depth direction. Place the left cuboid centered around (-2.4, 0.2) in screen/world layout. Place the right marginal panel to the right with a clear gap: rectangle about 4.1 units wide by 4.6 units high, centered around (+4.0, 0.2), so it is visually comparable in height to the cuboid rather than a small inset. Keep the probability labels below the panels: Pr(x, z | phi) centered under the cuboid and Pr(x | phi) centered under the right panel, both at least 0.55 units below the panel bottoms. Put the teal marginalization caption and arrow in the inter-panel gap around mid-height, not near the lower probability labels. Color palette: cuboid wireframe dark reddish brown #6b2d1a; text black #111111; arrow/caption teal #1c9a9a. Conditional curve colors, in increasing z order: red #d62728, green #2ca02c, blue #1f77b4, black #000000, olive #808000, magenta #e377c2, cyan #17becf, navy #000080, maroon #800000. Use z values [-2.0, -1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0]. Decoder mean path for positioning the conditional curves: mu(z) = (1.35 * sin(1.05 z) + 0.35 z, 0.85 * cos(0.95 z) - 0.25 z). For each z, draw a small curved elliptical contour in its x_1-x_2 slice: C_z(t) = mu(z) + R(theta(z)) * [0.55 cos(t), 0.28 sin(t)] with theta(z) = 0.7 z, t in [0, 2*pi]. In the left cuboid, place C_z at the corresponding oblique depth coordinate. In the right panel, draw the same C_z(t) in x_1-x_2 only, using the same color and line thickness. The right panel should show all projected colored curves simultaneously in sourceLayout. Do not include any posterior ridge, draggable observation point, current-z slice plane, z slider marker, or Pr(z | x, phi) label.
plan.notes: Render the cuboid and right panel with crisp line geometry or fat-line shaders so the textbook-style colored curves remain legible. Use CSS2D or signed-distance-field text for math labels. The viewStage interaction should only change visibility/layout emphasis: jointOnly hides the right panel and arrow, marginalOnly hides the left cuboid and arrow, and sourceLayout shows both panels plus the teal arrow and caption. The click interaction should not add new analytic objects; it only thickens or halos the selected color in both panels and may show a small z=value tag near that curve. Keep the default state as sourceLayout to match the static source figure.

authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the nonlinear latent variable model underlying a variational autoencoder (VAE), using two panels connected by a conceptual annotation. The left panel displays the joint distribution Pr(x, z|phi) in a three-dimensional coordinate system with axes x_1, x_2, and z, where a family of curved colored lines — rendered in multiple colors including red, green, blue, black, olive, magenta, cyan, navy, and maroon — represent the distribution of observed data x = (x_1, x_2) conditioned on each particular value of the scalar latent variable z; each color corresponds to a different z slice, and the nonlinear decoder network phi warps the latent axis into a curved manifold in data space. The right panel displays the marginal distribution Pr(x|phi) in the two-dimensional x_1-x_2 plane, obtained by integrating (marginalizing) over all values of the latent variable z; the same multi-colored curves now appear projected onto 2D, forming a complex non-Gaussian distribution that cannot be expressed in closed form. A label reading 'Marginalize over latent variable, z' with a teal arrow connects the two panels, indicating the mathematical operation that links them. The figure introduces the nonlinear latent variable generative model and motivates the need for variational inference, since the marginalization that links the joint distribution to the observable marginal is intractable.
authoredInteractions:
- Animate marginalization over z: show the joint distribution surface Pr(x, z|φ) in the x1–x2–z space collapsing along the z axis with a sweeping animation to produce the marginal Pr(x|φ) projected onto the x1–x2 plane
- Drag an input point (x1, x2): highlight the posterior distribution Pr(z|x, φ) for that observation on the z axis and show how the uncertainty in the latent variable z varies across different regions of the x1–x2 plane
- Slider for latent variable z value: move z along its axis and update the displayed slice of the joint distribution Pr(x, z|φ), revealing how the conditional Pr(x|z, φ) shifts position and shape across the x1–x2 plane

interactions.teaches: Rotating the scene clarifies that the dark panels are x_1-x_2 conditional slices positioned at different latent z values, not separate 2D plots.

interactions.label: Animate marginalization over z
interactions.teaches: The observable marginal Pr(x | phi) is formed by accumulating all conditional x_1-x_2 density slices across the latent z axis.

Moving an observed point x across the marginal density changes which latent z values plausibly generated it, revealing that the posterior Pr(z | x, phi) can be narrow, broad, or multimodal depending on location.

interactions.label: latent variable z
interactions.teaches: Changing z moves through conditional distributions Pr(x | z, phi); the decoder maps the one-dimensional latent coordinate into a curved path through the two-dimensional data space.

demo_steps.title: Joint latent-variable model
demo_steps.narration: The left cuboid shows Pr(x, z | phi). Each dark slice is an x_1-x_2 density at one latent value z, and the cyan curve follows the decoder's nonlinear mean through those slices.

demo_steps.title: Move along z
demo_steps.narration: Sliding z selects a different conditional slice Pr(x | z, phi). The bright density blob shifts nonlinearly across the x_1-x_2 plane instead of moving in a straight line.

demo_steps.title: Marginalize over the latent coordinate
demo_steps.narration: Run the marginalization animation to sweep along z and accumulate all slices. The result is the banana-shaped marginal density Pr(x | phi) shown on the right x_1-x_2 panel.

demo_steps.title: Infer z from an observed x
demo_steps.narration: Drag the teal observation point on the marginal panel. The highlighted posterior band along the z axis shows which latent values could have produced that observation and how uncertain that inverse mapping is.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an axonometric/isometric-style rendering with no perspective convergence. Left joint-space cuboid approximately 5.0 world units along x_1, 4.0 along x_2, and 5.0 along latent z. Treat x_1 as the horizontal coordinate inside each slice plane, x_2 as vertical, and z as the receding depth axis. Place the cuboid left of center, spanning roughly x_1 ∈ [-2.5, 2.5], x_2 ∈ [-2, 2], z ∈ [-2.5, 2.5]. Brown wireframe edges #7a351e, line width visually heavy. Slice planes are vertical x_1-x_2 rectangles at z ≈ -1.8, 0.0, and 1.4; each slice plane is dark reddish-brown #2a0702 with opacity about 0.9. Probability blobs on slices use a heatmap from dark brown #250602 through orange #b75a3a to cream #fff0bf, with soft radial/elliptical Gaussian falloff. A usable decoder mean curve is mu(z) = (x1, x2) = (1.35 * sin(1.15 z) + 0.35 z, -0.55 z + 1.1 * cos(1.0 z)); draw it as a thick cyan tube #9be0dc through the cuboid, with a dashed section where it passes behind the central slice. Conditional density may be p(x | z, phi) = N(x; mu(z), Sigma(z)), with Sigma(z) an anisotropic 2D covariance that rotates with z, e.g. principal stds 0.35 and 0.8. Use the prior p(z) = N(0, 1) truncated visually to [-2.5, 2.5], so the joint is p(x,z|phi)=p(x|z,phi)p(z). The right marginal panel is a separate flat x_1-x_2 rectangle to the right of the cuboid, about 2.2 world units wide by 3.2 high, slightly tilted to match the source; black border #000000. Its marginal heatmap is p(x|phi)=integral p(x|z,phi)p(z) dz over z, numerically sampled across the slider range. Place label 'Marginalize over latent variable, z' below the gap between panels with a large pale gray arrow #c8cfd0 pointing from left to right. Teal sample points are circles/spheres #2d8f8a with lighter outline #9be0dc.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement heatmaps as textured planes generated from a sampled density grid. For the marginal panel, precompute or dynamically integrate over 100-200 z samples. The marginalization animation should move a translucent cyan/white sweep plane along the cuboid z axis; as it advances, add the weighted conditional slice texture into the right-panel accumulation texture until the full marginal is visible. The latentZ slider updates the highlighted slice plane, the z-axis marker, and the conditional Gaussian texture on that plane. The draggable observation point should be constrained to the right x_1-x_2 panel; compute posterior weights w(z) proportional to p(x_drag | z, phi)p(z), normalize over sampled z, and display them as a glowing 1D density ribbon or stacked dots along the cuboid's z axis. Use billboarding or CSS2D labels for math text so labels remain legible while orbiting.

discrepancies: The overall composition is much smaller and more compressed than the source, with the right marginal panel too small relative to the cuboid and placed too close to it.
The generated figure adds an extra translucent current-z slice, posterior ridge/dots, z-axis marker, and Pr(z | x, φ) annotation that are not present in the source.
The main cuboid camera/view angle differs enough that the slice planes and cyan trajectory do not match the source's broad front-facing oblique layout.
The x2 label on the main cuboid is placed inside/near the top of the volume rather than clearly on the left vertical axis as in the source.
The large marginalization arrow and caption are present but visually cramped and partially overlap the lower labels, unlike the clear separated arrow/text in the source.
The heatmap panels and cyan curves are recognizable but their scale, positions, and occlusion relationship differ noticeably from the source.
evaluation.notes: The main latent-variable marginalization concept is recognizable and well-interactive, but the composition, scale, camera angle, label placement, and extra posterior elements reduce visual fidelity to the source.
action_items: Increase the size of the cuboid and especially the right marginal panel to better match the source proportions.
Adjust the initial orthographic camera/view so the cuboid has the same broad oblique perspective and clearer front-left/right depth relationship as the source.

Hide or remove the extra posterior ridge, current-z slice indicator, and Pr(z | x, φ) label when trying to match the static source figure.
plan_action_items: Decide whether the figure is meant to reproduce the source exactly or extend it with posterior-inference interactions; if exact reproduction is required, omit the posterior inference step and associated geometry.

feedback.rationale: Although the core concept is recognizable, the hallucinated posterior-inference elements stem from an incorrect or ambiguous plan extension, so the plan should be corrected before generation refinements.
